title: Yamaguchi Akane falls to Ashmita Chaliha, opens path for Ahn Se-young - CHOSUNBIZ
text:
Yamaguchi Akane falls to Ashmita Chaliha, opens path for Ahn Se-young - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 23일(금) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Yamaguchi Akane falls to Ashmita Chaliha, opens path for Ahn Se-young 
 입력 2026.10.23. 00:40 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 "'Japan's badminton pride' Yamaguchi Akane (29·world No. 2) suffered a shocking upset. After recently fiercely contesting with Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) and losing all encounters, she did not even get the chance to meet Ahn Se-young this time."
 Yamaguchi on the 22nd (Korea time) lost in the round of 16 of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour French Open women's singles at Arena Grand Paris in Paris, France, to world No. 36 Ashmita Chaliha (India) by a game score of 0-2 (19-21, 18-21).
 Yamaguchi, defeated in 37 minutes, packed her bags early. If she had continued to win, she could have met Ahn Se-young in the semifinals. But with Yamaguchi's early exit, Ahn Se-young can feel less pressure ahead of the final.
 In the first game Yamaguchi appeared to seize the momentum by leading 18-14. But she conceded four consecutive points to allow an 18-18 tie and never regained control, eventually losing 19-21.
 She could not recover in the second game either. At 7-7 Yamaguchi collapsed, conceding six straight points. She later scored four consecutive points to set up a comeback attempt, but that was all. In the end she failed to close a three-point gap and was eliminated.
 Yamaguchi is a long-time rival who has faced Ahn Se-young many times. However, recently she has suffered 10 straight losses to Ahn Se-young. She lost in the final of the 2026 Aichi–Nagoya Asian Games, and on the 18th she also lost a comeback defeat 1-2 in the Denmark Open final.
 Even so, Yamaguchi delivered a classic match by pushing Ahn Se-young into a corner with aggressive play. The Denmark Open final was a brutal fight that lasted as long as 1 hour and 17 minutes. Ahn Se-young trailed 5-11 in the final game at the interval, but she summoned tremendous resilience and kissed the winner's trophy.
 That is why the 'loser' Yamaguchi also received applause. Commentators for the BWF and fans watching the match praised it as one of the best matches. On Chinese communities there were evaluations such as "Yamaguchi today was a 100 out of 100."
 Although Yamaguchi narrowly missed the title, she reclaimed the world No. 2 ranking by finishing runner-up at the Denmark Open, surpassing the previous world No. 2 Wang Zhiyi (China). She was expected to fight a real battle with Ahn Se-young for a place in the French Open final, but she was caught by Chaliha, who is recording a career high.
 Meanwhile, Ahn Se-young earlier dismissed the challenge of India's prodigious youngster Tanvi Sharma (world No. 24) in the round of 16, winning 2-0 (21-11, 21-14). In the quarterfinals she will face China's Han Wei (world No. 10).
 With Yamaguchi's elimination, Ahn Se-young's chance of a third straight French Open title has grown. She won the tournament in 2024 and 2025 as well.
 If Ahn Se-young were to win the France Open following the Denmark Open, it would be her 48th career title. With the Denmark Open win she reached 47 career titles, surpassing Indonesia's legend Susi Susanti to set a new record for most women's singles titles. Each additional title going forward would be a new piece of history.
 Also, for Ahn Se-young, who has already secured nine wins this season, it would be her 10th title of the season. She is just one win shy of last year's record for most women's singles wins in a single season (11). She looks poised to comfortably surpass the single-season record of 11 wins by Japan's men's singles star Momota Kento set in 2019.
